rationale: Evidence: all 300 development trials so far ended off_track with no finishes. The best design is iteration 7 (score 125.3): 12 mm footprints, five sensors at x = -0.02 to +0.02 (10 mm spacing), y = 0.03, kp 3.0, ki 0.4, kd 0.35, base 1.3, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12. Iteration 8 changed two things at once (kp 3.5 and wheel_track 0.11) and scored lower (108.4). Its s-bend progress fell from 0.23 to 0.12 and line-loss events rose to 2, so I revert both changes and keep the iteration 7 controller. Max_error still reaches about 0.06 to 0.066 with 1 to 2 line-loss events per run, so the robot loses the tape at bends before the search can recover. The 12 mm footprint improved results (iteration 7 versus 6, +9.5), which suggests that the detectable tape edge matters. Changing one variable at a time, I widen the footprint to 16 mm (the largest allowed) with everything else as in iteration 7. A larger footprint should see the tape edge from further off-centre, so the line is held longer and the search starts from a better position. Expected result: line_loss_events at 1 or fewer on oval and s-bend, max_error below 0.06 on oval, and progress at or above 0.6 on oval. Hypotheses: H1, the 16 mm footprint extends the detection window at the cost of some edge resolution. H2, kp 3.0 with kd 0.35 is adequate once the sensing is improved. Measurements needed next: line_loss_events and max_error per track, to see whether the loss moves or disappears; steering_oscillation, to check for jitter from the coarser signal; and progress and completion_time on s-bend and slalom. If the 16 mm footprint reduces progress or raises oscillation, return to 12 mm and test base_speed 1.4 instead.
